note: #519 (ClickUp 86bc7g0uz, founder go 2026-09-25) persists the signup newsletter choice on users/{uid} (newsletterOptIn, newsletterOptInAt, newsletterOptInSource, written only at account creation, no backfill), adds a founder-only Newsletter filter and a server-side super-admin CSV export (/api/admin/crm-export) to the platform-wide CRM, and locks the three consent fields in firestore.rules against later edits by the member or a church admin. This record carries the firestore.rules digest because this ticket DOES change that file, and firestore.rules auto-deploys on merge: merge needs explicit founder go.

entries.why: #519 owns this change and it is the users match block only: a new newsletterConsentOnCreate() check validates newsletterOptIn (bool), newsletterOptInAt (== request.time) and newsletterOptInSource ('signup-email' or 'signup-google') when a user creates their own doc, and the three keys join both the self-edit and the tenant-admin affectedKeys deny lists so neither a member nor a church admin can rewrite consent after signup. The super-admin branch and every other match block are byte-identical. Proven by 6 new emulator tests in tests/rules/users.rules.test.ts.

#519 owns this change: the pre-ticked newsletter switch moves above the Google button on the signup tab, both account-creation paths write newsletterOptIn / newsletterOptInAt (serverTimestamp) / newsletterOptInSource at create time (true and false alike), the legacy newsletter write is gone, and both sign-in updateDoc calls now write termsAccepted only.

#519 owns this change: in the platform-wide super-admin CRM view only, a Newsletter segmented filter (All / Opted in / Opted out / Unknown) ANDed with search and Type, and an Export CSV button that calls /api/admin/crm-export with the same filters and the caller's ID token. Church-admin tenant views render neither control; the existing Signups export is untouched.

#519 owns this change: the contact/user merge moves verbatim into src/lib/crm-merge.ts so the server export route runs the exact same merge, and this hook imports and re-exports it. Contact gains an optional accountProfile (tenantId, createdAt, newsletterOptIn/At/Source) carried from the users doc; queries and caching are unchanged.

#519 owns ONE widened regex in this file and the comment that says why: the directory sweep now accepts a per-ticket record named `#nnn.json` as well as `THE-nnn.json`, which is exactly the pair of spellings loadOwnership's TICKET_RE already accepts as a ticket and that THE-325's CONTENT_ASSERTING_MOVED table already uses for #517. Still one file per ticket and still no index; every other assertion, count and entry is byte-identical.
